toegepas.rede_vinder: Saammeng is a compound verb in AWS spelling, so the participle is written as one word.
toegepas.fout: The participle of the separable compound verb saammeng is written apart.
toegepas.rede_keurder: AWS writes saamgemeng as one word; the meaning is unchanged and the protected sentence elsewhere is not touched.

toegepas.voor: Om 'n vaste stof in 'n vloeistof te meng is
toegepas.na: Om 'n vaste stof in 'n vloeistof te meng, is
toegepas.rede_vinder: A comma after a long opening om...te clause that acts as the subject makes the sentence easier to read.
toegepas.fout: A long om...te clause acting as subject runs straight into the main verb without a pause.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma marks where the subject clause ends and makes the sentence easier to read on first pass.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Mag for possibility copies English 'may'; Afrikaans uses kan here.
toegepas.fout: Mag for possibility copies English 'may' and can be read as permission.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Kan is the natural Afrikaans for possibility and the meaning stays the same.

toegepas.rede_vinder: En joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma.
toegepas.fout: Missing comma before en joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: AWS 2017 house rule requires the comma here; the protected wording stays intact.

toegepas.voor: oral in die tee al sien
toegepas.na: oral in die tee, al sien
toegepas.rede_vinder: A comma before the concessive al-clause separates it clearly from the main clause.
toegepas.fout: The concessive al-clause runs into the main clause without a separating comma.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma separates main clause and concessive clause and helps the reader without moving the meaning.

toegepas.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
toegepas.voor: Die water word troebel en jy kan
toegepas.na: Die water word troebel, en jy kan
toegepas.rede_vinder: En joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma; the protected wording stays intact.
toegepas.fout: Missing comma before en joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: AWS 2017 house rule requires the comma; the protected wording after it is left whole.

toegepas.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
toegepas.voor: Die ondersoek toets wat jy sien nadat jy
toegepas.na: In die ondersoek let jy op wat jy sien nadat jy
toegepas.rede_vinder: An investigation does not 'test what you see'; the learner observes, so the sentence reads wooden as it stands.
toegepas.fout: An investigation 'testing what you see' is wooden; the learner is the one who observes.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal is natural Afrikaans and keeps the same criterion, observation after stirring a teaspoon into water.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Totdat is the standard written conjunction; tot as a conjunction is more colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Tot as a conjunction is standard, natural Afrikaans, so totdat is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Dit lyk asof is the more standard written form than dit lyk of.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Dit lyk of is standard Afrikaans and reads naturally, so asof is only different.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Totdat is the standard written conjunction; tot as a conjunction is more colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Tot as a conjunction is standard and natural, and dropping it matches decision 3.

vlae.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
vlae.teks: Die ondersoek toets wat jy sien
vlae.rede: 'Die ondersoek' is definite but no investigation is introduced earlier in the lesson; if it refers to a practical outside the text, the reference may be unclear to a learner reading the text alone. Not changed beyond the proposed wording fix, because the intended referent is content.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Vir oplos het jy twee stowwe nodig wat saam gemeng word
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: AWS 2017 writes the compound verb saammeng as one word, so 'saam gemeng' should be 'saamgemeng'; the protected wording keeps a spelling error, and it now differs from the proposed fix in the first block.
